## Meta-review synthesis

Across three rounds the loop converged on the defining clinical reality of diffuse unpatterned alopecia: it is a diagnosis of exclusion, and the highest-yield interventions are the ones that respect that structure rather than the highest-Elo systemic bets. The final Elo table is stratified almost exactly along this line. The top tier (1547-1548) is occupied entirely by one lineage - the biomarker-gated micronutrient correction protocol (H008 -> H013 -> H028 -> H040) - whose final lean form H040 drops the structurally underpowered L-lysine arm and demotes the contested 40-70 ng/mL ferritin range from a claimed therapeutic threshold to an operational trigger under interventional test. External validation is what makes H040 the lead pick: zero prior alopecia trials, PubMed novelty score 1.0, confidence 3, verified associational citations (PMIDs 20021982, 32792884, 16635664, 24887725), near-zero cost, and a safety case that IS the gating (no iron in non-deficient patients without a source-of-loss workup). The single strongest near-term experiment in the whole run is simply executing H040: a 16-week repletion trial in confirmed-deficient diffuse-loss patients with shed count and standardized densitometry endpoints versus a non-deficient reference arm. It tests whether the entire deficiency-mimic thesis is causal, cheaply, and the answer re-routes a large patient fraction either way.

For the true androgen-driven remnant, H041 is the right final form of the androgen lineage: it merges H001 and H002 into a sequential program (topical/low-dose dutasteride first with a densitometry futility threshold, oral escalation, then topical bicalutamide only behind a preclinical skin-PK gate). Validation cuts both ways here and the synthesis should be candid about it: dutasteride has the strongest disease-target overlap in the run (SRD5A2 0.70, SRD5A1 0.51, SRD5A3 0.50 via OpenTargets) but also 10 prior alopecia trials up to phase 4 and 280 PubMed co-mentions - it is validated pharmacology, not a novel bet, and the dossier itself warns 5AR-inhibitor response in DUPA is anecdotal and probably attenuated. H042 (final adenosine form) earns its pick as the best-evidenced mechanism-agnostic anagen support after minoxidil - an approved AGA product in Japan with RCT data, topical safety scored 9 by reviewers - but the loop was honest that its expected effect is maintenance-level, not reversal, and its industry-run Japanese patterned-AGA evidence base does not transfer cleanly to DUPA. H035 (TSH-gated levothyroxine) is the cheapest completeness pick: it closes the last uncovered exclusion niche (the thyroid mimic, PMID 38181279) with confidence 3 and benign lab-guided dosing. H043 is included as portfolio plumbing rather than a repurposing bet - its own review concedes zero novelty (349 co-mentions, approved AA pharmacology) - but the double-gated incognita rule-out arm is the only entry preventing autoimmune mimics from being misrouted into androgen-axis trials, and in a diagnosis-of-exclusion disease that routing has real expected value.

Where the loop is confident: the exclusion-workup architecture (deficiency, endocrine, incognita arms) and the exposure-minimization logic for androgen-axis therapy. Where it is guessing: everything mechanistic beyond those anchors. The oxidative-stress axis (H044) is two unproven inferences deep and survives only as a Stage-A pharmacodynamic gate; nicorandil, fluridil, estradiol, and metformin never rose above Elo 1508 for good reason. The tournament also visibly could not separate within lineages - H008/H013/H028/H040 sit within 1 Elo point, and the 1532 tier is a six-way tie of three lineages - so within-lineage ranking is noise and the picks above deliberately take one final form per lineage. The most efficient discriminating experiments, in order: (1) the H040 repletion trial, which tests causality of the strongest associational signal; (2) a densitometry-stratified topical dutasteride pilot with a predefined futility threshold, which tests the dossier's leading model of androgen-driven DUPA directly; (3) scalp glutathione-redox pharmacodynamics after oral NAC (H044 Stage A), a cheap kill-or-continue gate for the entire oxidative-stress axis. Limitations: this is prioritization, not proof - no hypothesis in the run has DUPA-stratified interventional evidence, several validations carry no chembl_id or errored OpenTargets lookups (nutrients, protocols, nicorandil, NAC), novelty scores for renamed evolved entries (novelty 1.0 for H029/H040-H044) partly reflect name-matching artifacts rather than true literature absence, and Elo differences within 16 points should be treated as ties.

**Themes:** Diagnosis-of-exclusion mimic capture via biomarker-gated correction: ferritin/25(OH)D repletion (H008 -> H013 -> H028 -> H040), TSH-gated levothyroxine (H035), and zinc as screening-only, targeting the CTE/deficiency/endocrine mimics of the diffuse-thinning presentation rather than true androgen-driven DUPA; Androgen-axis suppression with exposure minimization for densitometry-confirmed true androgen-driven DUPA: topical-first dutasteride with a futility threshold, escalating to oral 0.5 mg and then preclinical-gated topical bicalutamide (H001/H002 merged into H041; combination variant H027); Mechanism-agnostic anagen support with honestly bounded expectations: topical adenosine 0.75% as maintenance-level support, not miniaturization reversal (H017 -> H029 -> H042), alongside the minoxidil SULT1A1 bioactivation bottleneck (H036) and its tretinoin adjunct (H006); Autoimmune mimic capture: double-gated (biopsy plus concordant clinical picture) short-course oral JAK inhibition strictly for diffuse alopecia areata incognita, with ambiguous cases defaulting to no immunosuppression (H019 -> H032 -> H043); Exploratory mechanistic axes admitted only through pharmacodynamic gates with kill criteria: biomarker-stratified N-acetylcysteine oxidative-stress pilot (H023 -> H044), KATP-openers (nicorandil H003), and hemorheologic/anti-inflammatory adjuncts (pentoxifylline H022/H030)

**Top picks:** H040, H042, H041, H035, H043

## Candidate details

### 1. iron (ferrous sulfate) (H008)

- ChEMBL: n/a | Elo 1548 | confidence 3/5 | route: oral | origin: generation (round 1)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: the deficiency-mimic / chronic telogen effluvium sub-population of the diffuse-thinning presentation - specifically patients with confirmed low ferritin - rather than true androgen-driven DUPA. The hair matrix is among the most proliferative tissues in the body and is exquisitely sensitive to iron availability; low iron stores (even without anemia) impair ribonucleotide reductase and matrix keratinocyte proliferation, shortening anagen and increasing telogen shedding. Oral ferrous sulfate repletion, dosed to a target ferritin and paired with a source-of-loss workup, removes a treatable driver of diffuse shedding that otherwise masquerades as DUPA.
- **Evidence:** PMID 20021982: women with diffuse telogen hair loss had significantly lower ferritin (16.3 vs 60.3 ng/mL) and transferrin saturation than matched controls. PMID 32792884: mean ferritin significantly lower in diffuse-hair-loss patients vs healthy controls (14.72 vs 25.30 ng/mL); authors recommend ferritin evaluation before treatment. PMID 16635664: review of iron deficiency and its potential relationship to hair loss, with ferritin as the confirmatory test. This is a biomarker-stratified correction hypothesis, per the dossier's guidance. (refs: PMID 16635664, PMID 20021982, PMID 32792884)
- **Safety:** The dossier warns against blind supplementation: excess iron is harmful and inappropriate in non-deficient men and postmenopausal women, where iron deficiency also mandates a GI blood-loss workup (PMID 16635664). Hypothesis is explicitly gated on confirmed low ferritin with a defined repletion target and monitoring; GI upset and constipation are the common tolerability issues.
- **Novelty rationale:** Not novel as a concept - iron-hair associations are long-studied - but the hypothesis is the evidence-graded version the dossier asks for: a ferritin-stratified correction protocol within the diagnostic-exclusion workup, not blind supplementation. Its role in the portfolio is to capture the large, treatable mimic population.

Reviews:
- plausibility 8/10, evidence 6/10, safety 7/10, novelty 2/10 — verdict **accept**. Citations check out: PMIDs 20021982, 32792884, and 16635664 all exist in the corpus, and the quoted ferritin figures (16.3 vs 60.3 ng/mL in 20021982; 14.72 vs 25.30 ng/mL in 32792884) match the abstracts. The hypothesis is exactly the evidence-graded, deficiency-gated correction the dossier asks for, and it correctly handles the overload/workup hazards. Two honest weaknesses: (1) this is standard-of-care diagnostic exclusion, not drug repurposing — its novelty is nil and the hypothesis admits it; (2) the evidence is purely associational — even the cited 20021982 abstract notes 'relatively discrepant findings' in the literature, and there is no solid interventional evidence that ferritin repletion to any target restores density in CTE, so 'removes a treatable driver' overstates what is proven. Accepted anyway because the portfolio needs the mimic-population capture and the gating, target-ferritin, and source-of-loss-workup constraints are specified correctly; it should be tracked as a workup/correction entry, not scored alongside true repurposing bets.

### 2. biomarker-gated micronutrient repletion protocol with defined ferritin target (ferrous sulfate to ferritin 40-70 ng/mL + cholecalciferol, with randomized L-lysine adjunct arm for iron partial responders) (H028)

- ChEMBL: n/a | Elo 1548 | confidence 3/5 | route: oral | origin: evolution (round 2)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: the deficiency-mimic / chronic telogen effluvium sub-population - patients with confirmed low ferritin and/or low 25-hydroxyvitamin D - explicitly not true androgen-driven DUPA and not non-deficient patients. This evolution's material change is to replace the parent's undefined 'target ferritin per protocol' with a committed, checkable number: repletion to a ferritin of 40-70 ng/mL (the range the diffuse-loss literature associates with reduced shedding, stated as a protocol target while acknowledging the dossier flags the causal threshold as debated), reassessed at 16 weeks. Iron deficiency impairs ribonucleotide reductase and matrix keratinocyte proliferation, shortening anagen; vitamin D insufficiency is repleted to 25(OH)D normalization on the same schedule. The lysine question is hardened into the exact design the H012 reviewer requested: confirmed-deficient patients who fail to reach the ferritin target at 16 weeks on iron alone (partial responders) are randomized to continued iron versus iron + L-lysine (1-1.5 g/day, exploiting lysine's facilitation of intestinal iron absorption and cellular uptake), with non-deficient patients excluded at baseline. Zinc survives only as high-risk screening (post-bariatric, malabsorption) with copper monitoring, per the folded zinc salvage.
- **Evidence:** Unchanged associational base, cited accurately: PMID 20021982 (ferritin 16.3 vs 60.3 ng/mL in diffuse telogen hair loss vs controls; notes 'relatively discrepant findings'), PMID 32792884 (ferritin 14.72 vs 25.30 ng/mL and lower 25(OH)D in diffuse loss vs controls; authors recommend evaluating both), PMID 16635664 (ferritin as confirmatory test; warns against supplementation without confirmed deficiency), PMID 24887725 (zinc normal in most shedders - why zinc is screening-only). The reviews' grading stands and is now built into the protocol: no citation shows repletion restores density, so the protocol's primary endpoint is explicitly interventional (change in shed count/density after repletion to the defined target), converting the associational weakness into the tested question. The lysine arm's only prior human data are old, small, and industry-adjacent (Rushton), not in the provided corpus - stated, and exactly why it is a randomized sub-arm rather than a claim. (refs: PMID 16635664, PMID 20021982, PMID 32792884, PMID 24887725)
- **Safety:** Gating on confirmed deficiency remains the safety mechanism: no iron in non-deficient men or postmenopausal women without a GI source-of-loss workup (PMID 16635664); cholecalciferol at monitored repletion doses; L-lysine at gram-range doses is benign; zinc restricted to confirmed deficiency in high-risk patients with copper monitoring. The defined 40-70 ng/mL ceiling also bounds iron exposure, avoiding overshoot in a cosmetic context.
- **Novelty rationale:** Materially changed from H013: the review's central objection - the undefined ferritin target, 'exactly the number that decides who gets treated' - is fixed by committing to 40-70 ng/mL with a 16-week checkpoint, and the 'softest component' (lysine) is converted from an asserted adjunct into the H012 reviewer's requested randomized lysine+iron versus iron-alone comparison in confirmed partial responders. The protocol is now fully specified end-to-end: baseline panel, defined targets, defined reassessment interval, defined escalation randomization. It remains a workup/correction layer, tracked as such, not a repurposing bet - that framing from the H013 review is preserved.

Reviews:
- plausibility 7/10, evidence 4/10, safety 9/10, novelty 4/10 — verdict **accept**. All four cited PMIDs verified in the corpus and quoted accurately (20021982: ferritin 16.3 vs 60.3 ng/mL and the 'relatively discrepant findings' caveat match verbatim; 32792884: 14.72 vs 25.30 ng/mL matches; 16635664 and 24887725 correctly characterized). The problem is not attribution but what the evidence is: two small case-control associations, zero interventional data showing repletion to any ferritin target restores density. The 40-70 ng/mL target, now 'committed', is still an arbitrary point in a contested literature - committing to a number does not make the number right, and the hypothesis concedes this. The lysine sub-arm rests on old, small, industry-adjacent Rushton data and will enroll only partial responders of an already-gated sub-population, so it is structurally underpowered to answer the question it poses. Weakest link overall: this is standard deficiency workup dressed as a research protocol - defensible and honest, but its ceiling is clinical hygiene, not repurposing. ### 4. biomarker-gated micronutrient repletion protocol (ferrous sulfate + cholecalciferol, with L-lysine adjunct for iron partial responders) (H013)

- ChEMBL: n/a | Elo 1547 | confidence 3/5 | route: oral | origin: evolution (round 1)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: the deficiency-mimic / chronic telogen effluvium sub-population of the diffuse-thinning presentation - patients with confirmed low ferritin and/or low 25-hydroxyvitamin D - not true androgen-driven DUPA, and explicitly not non-deficient patients. The hair matrix is among the most proliferative tissues in the body: iron deficiency impairs ribonucleotide reductase and matrix keratinocyte proliferation, shortening anagen and increasing telogen shedding, and vitamin D insufficiency is repeatedly associated with diffuse loss. The merged protocol is a staged workup, not blind supplementation: (1) baseline panel of ferritin and 25(OH)D in every diffuse-loss presentation; zinc measured only in high-risk patients (post-bariatric, malabsorption, protein-calorie malnutrition), with copper monitoring if zinc is repleted - the salvageable core of the rejected zinc hypothesis, whose own citations showed zinc deficiency in only a small minority of shedders and no zinc difference vs controls; (2) repletion of confirmed deficiencies to defined targets (target ferritin per protocol, 25(OH)D normalization), paired with a source-of-loss workup for iron deficiency in men and postmenopausal women; (3) L-lysine added only in iron-monotherapy partial responders (ferritin failing to reach target at a defined interval), exploiting lysine's facilitation of intestinal iron absorption and cellular uptake. Repletion removes treatable drivers of diffuse shedding that otherwise masquerade as DUPA.
- **Evidence:** PMID 20021982: women with diffuse telogen hair loss had significantly lower ferritin (16.3 vs 60.3 ng/mL) and transferrin saturation than matched controls. PMID 32792884: diffuse-loss patients had significantly lower mean ferritin (14.72 vs 25.30 ng/mL) and lower 25-hydroxyvitamin D than controls; the authors recommend evaluating both before treatment - the direct basis for the combined panel. PMID 16635664: review supporting ferritin as the confirmatory test and warning against supplementation without confirmed deficiency. PMID 24887725 (folded zinc content): mean zinc was normal even in shedders (only 3 of 42 deficient), post-surgical shedding was linked to rapid weight loss, and the strongest signal was combined zinc+iron - which is why zinc survives only as high-risk screening with copper monitoring, not as standalone supplementation. Honest grading per the peer reviews: all evidence is associational (20021982 itself notes 'relatively discrepant findings'), and there is no solid interventional proof that repletion to any target restores density; this entry should be tracked as a workup/correction protocol, not scored alongside true repurposing bets. (refs: PMID 16635664, PMID 20021982, PMID 32792884, PMID 24887725)
- **Safety:** Gating on confirmed deficiency is the safety mechanism: excess iron is harmful in non-deficient men and postmenopausal women, where deficiency also mandates a GI blood-loss workup (PMID 16635664); cholecalciferol at monitored repletion doses has a wide margin with hypercalcemia risk only at high unmonitored doses; L-lysine at gram-range doses is benign. Zinc is restricted to confirmed deficiency in high-risk patients with copper monitoring, avoiding the narrow-therapeutic-window problem (excess zinc harms hair and depletes copper) that contributed to the zinc standalone hypothesis's rejection. Common tolerability issues: GI upset/constipation for iron.
- **Novelty rationale:** Materially changed from all three parents: this is the single combined micronutrient-correction hypothesis the H009 reviewer explicitly requested ('fold it into a single combined micronutrient-correction hypothesis with H008'), with the H012 reviewer's requested design built in - lysine+iron versus iron alone in confirmed-deficient partial responders, with non-deficient patients excluded. It also folds in the rejected zinc hypothesis's salvageable content (high-risk-deficiency screening with copper monitoring) as a screening arm only, exactly as that review instructed. What is new is the staged, biomarker-gated protocol with defined repletion targets and a stratified partial-responder adjunct arm - not any single nutrient claim, which the reviews correctly graded as associational and non-novel.

Reviews:
- plausibility 7/10, evidence 6/10, safety 9/10, novelty 5/10 — verdict **accept**. Citation check: all four PMIDs (20021982, 32792884, 16635664, 24887725) exist in the corpus and are accurately characterized, including the honest caveats (20021982's 'relatively discrepant findings'; 24887725's normal mean zinc with only 3/42 deficient). Weakest links: (1) every citation is associational case-control or observational work in telogen-effluvium/deficiency populations, none in trichoscopy-confirmed DUPA, and none shows repletion restores density - the hypothesis admits this but still asks to be 'tracked as a workup protocol', i.e., it is standard-of-care diagnostic hygiene, not a repurposing bet, and it does nothing for the true androgen-driven DUPA core of the problem; (2) the ferritin repletion target is left undefined ('per protocol'), and the contested causal threshold (the dossier flags this as debated) is exactly the number that decides who gets treated; (3) the L-lysine partial-responder arm rests on old, small, largely industry-adjacent human data - as a stratified sub-arm it is defensible, but it is the softest component. Safety-by-gating is genuine and correctly handles the iron-in-men and zinc/copper problems. Accept as a mandatory workup layer, with the explicit understanding that it addresses mimics, not DUPA itself.

### 5. adenosine (H017)

- ChEMBL: CHEMBL477 | Elo 1532 | confidence 3/5 | route: topical | origin: generation (round 2)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: mechanism-agnostic anagen support applicable to all DUPA sub-populations, positioned as an alternative for patients who cannot use or do not respond to KATP-opener therapy. Topical adenosine acts on adenosine receptors in dermal papilla cells, upregulating FGF7 (and reportedly VEGF) and prolonging anagen; it is not a prodrug and has no SULT1A1 bioactivation requirement, so it is orthogonal to the minoxidil-response bottleneck the incumbents attack.
- **Evidence:** Adenosine is approved for AGA in Japan with controlled trials showing increased thick-hair ratio (flagged as prior hair use). The dossier supports mechanism-agnostic anagen support as valid regardless of miniaturization driver. No provided excerpt addresses it; DUPA-specific evidence is absent. (refs: none)
- **Safety:** Topical adenosine (0.75% lotion in Japanese studies) is very well tolerated with minimal systemic exposure; oral/systemic adenosine effects (transient AV block, flushing) are irrelevant at topical scalp doses. Suitable safety profile for a cosmetic indication.
- **Novelty rationale:** Prior hair indication in Japan is flagged, not hidden. Novelty within this run: a non-KATP, non-androgen, growth-factor-axis anagen support with actual controlled human hair data - a mechanism class no incumbent occupies (nicorandil is KATP; dutasteride/bicalutamide are androgen-axis).

Reviews:
- plausibility 6/10, evidence 4/10, safety 9/10, novelty 5/10 — verdict **revise**. The strongest of the uncited generation entries, but still uncited: the claimed Japanese approval and controlled trials (0.75% lotion, increased thick-hair ratio in male AGA - the Shiseido program) are real but must be actually cited, and the effect sizes were modest, in patterned AGA, mostly Japanese men, with some industry involvement. Two specific weaknesses: (1) the differentiator 'no SULT1A1 requirement, orthogonal to the minoxidil bottleneck' is a marketing point, not evidence - there is no data showing adenosine rescues minoxidil non-responders, so the claimed niche is asserted rather than demonstrated; (2) mechanism-agnostic anagen prolongation (FGF7/VEGF in dermal papilla) does not address the miniaturization driver, so in true DUPA the honest expectation is the same partial, maintenance-level benefit minoxidil gives, not reversal of occipital miniaturization - the hypothesis should say so. Safety and cosmetic acceptability are excellent. Revise to add the actual trial citations, drop or soften the non-responder claim, and frame it as a second anagen-support option alongside (not instead of) the KATP class.

The class concept (topical AR antagonist for androgen-driven loss) is no longer novel: fluridil, pyrilutamide, and clascoterone have already established topical AR-antagonist feasibility in hair, so the only new element is the specific drug, and no rationale is given for bicalutamide over agents with better-characterized topical profiles. The teratogenicity/contraception caveat for women of childbearing potential undercuts the claim that this route suits the very sub-population (women) it nominally targets. No citations at all. Needs a comparative justification of molecule choice and preclinical skin-pharmacokinetic data before any human rationale.

### 15. tretinoin (H006)

- ChEMBL: CHEMBL38 | Elo 1516 | confidence 3/5 | route: topical (combination with minoxidil, with titration protocol) | origin: generation (round 1)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: assay-confirmed SULT1A1-low minoxidil non-responders with diffuse thinning (any DUPA sub-population), enrolled only after failing a defined minoxidil trial. Primary mechanism (downgraded claim, per the review): tretinoin enhances percutaneous penetration of co-applied minoxidil and normalizes follicular keratinization - established dermatology pharmacology that needs no unsupported citation. Secondary mechanism (now explicitly a test, not an assertion): whether topical tretinoin upregulates follicular SULT1A1, measured directly by plucked-hair SULT1A1 activity assay before and during treatment. Protocol: tretinoin 0.01% titrated to 0.025% as tolerated, co-applied with minoxidil 5%; response conversion defined as a prespecified regrowth endpoint (e.g., >=10% increase in target-area terminal hair count at 24 weeks) with the SULT1A1 assay as the mechanistic readout. The unsupported 'more valuable in DUPA' rhetoric is dropped; DUPA relevance is stated plainly as mechanism-agnostic anagen support where androgen-axis options underperform.
- **Evidence:** The dossier documents SULT1A1 dependence of minoxidil response and the existence of non-responders. Retinoid enhancement of percutaneous penetration and retinoid-minoxidil combination use in AGA since the 1980s are established - flagged as pre-existing, not novel. No provided citation supports SULT1A1 induction by tretinoin; that claim is therefore carried as a measured secondary endpoint rather than an evidence claim, exactly as the reviewer required. (refs: none)
- **Safety:** Topical tretinoin causes predictable local irritation, peeling, and photosensitivity, managed by the low-start titration (0.01% to 0.025%). Strict avoidance in pregnancy. Minimal systemic absorption from scalp application. Topical-only at low concentration, since oral retinoids cause drug-induced telogen effluvium (dossier).
- **Novelty rationale:** Materially changed per the review's two salvage conditions: (a) the SULT1A1-induction claim is downgraded from an asserted mechanism to a directly assayed secondary endpoint (plucked-hair SULT1A1 activity), with penetration enhancement as the citation-free primary mechanism; (b) concentration (0.01% to 0.025% titration), population selection (assay-confirmed SULT1A1-low non-responders only), and response-conversion measurement (defined regrowth endpoint plus enzyme assay) are now specified. The DUPA-specific overclaim is removed.

Reviews:
- plausibility 7/10, evidence 4/10, safety 7/10, novelty 3/10 — verdict **revise**. The weakest link is novelty, and it is close to fatal: tretinoin-plus-minoxidil is one of the oldest combination tricks in the AGA playbook (in use since the 1980s, originally justified by percutaneous-penetration enhancement), so the 'new combination rationale' exception is doing heavy lifting. The genuinely fresher angle — tretinoin upregulating follicular SULT1A1 to rescue minoxidil non-responders — is asserted without a single citation; the hypothesis provides zero source_refs, and the dossier only documents SULT1A1 dependence, not retinoid induction of the enzyme. The DUPA-specific justification is also thin: there is no evidence that SULT1A1-low non-response is more prevalent or more consequential in DUPA than in patterned AGA, so 'more valuable in DUPA' is rhetoric. Salvageable if revised to (a) cite the actual sulfotransferase-induction literature or downgrade the claim to penetration enhancement, and (b) specify concentration, titration, and how response conversion would be measured (e.g., follicular SULT1A1 assay or a defined regrowth endpoint).

### 16. vitamin D (cholecalciferol) (H009)

- ChEMBL: n/a | Elo 1516 | confidence 2/5 | route: oral | origin: generation (round 1)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: diffuse-loss patients with confirmed low 25-hydroxyvitamin D - a deficiency-associated sub-population overlapping CTE and diffuse thinning rather than strictly androgen-driven DUPA. Beyond the receptor-level rationale (VDR is essential for follicle cycling), systemic vitamin D repletion corrects the deficient state that is repeatedly found associated with diffuse hair loss; the hypothesis is biomarker-gated supplementation with 25(OH)D measurement before and during treatment, testing whether normalization of levels coincides with reduced shedding and improved density.
- **Evidence:** PMID 32792884: mean serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was significantly lower in diffuse-hair-loss patients than in healthy controls, alongside lower ferritin; the study's conclusion is that both should be evaluated before treatment. The dossier grades supplementation evidence as strongest when a true deficiency exists and weak-to-absent for supplementing the replete - this hypothesis adopts that gating explicitly. (refs: PMID 32792884)
- **Safety:** Oral cholecalciferol at repletion doses has a wide safety margin; hypercalcemia risk arises only at high doses without monitoring. Biomarker-gated dosing with follow-up levels keeps risk minimal and matches the cosmetic-indication tolerance profile.
- **Novelty rationale:** Association-level evidence exists (flagged); what is missing - and proposed here - is a deficiency-stratified interventional design in the diffuse-loss population rather than undifferentiated supplementation. Distinct from the topical calcitriol hypothesis, which targets follicular VDR signaling directly.

Reviews:
- plausibility 6/10, evidence 4/10, safety 9/10, novelty 2/10 — verdict **revise**. PMID 32792884 verifies, and the claim (lower 25(OH)D and ferritin in diffuse-loss patients; recommendation to evaluate both before treatment) is accurately represented — but note that study is a small (n=54) retrospective comparison that establishes association only. The mechanistic leg is weaker than presented: VDR's essential role in follicle cycling is demonstrated mainly by receptor-knockout biology (hereditary vitamin-D-resistant rickets alopecia), which does not imply that correcting modest systemic insufficiency reverses diffuse shedding — and there is essentially no controlled interventional evidence that repletion improves hair outcomes in deficient diffuse-loss patients. So the proposal is association-graded supplementation with a trial design stapled on. It is also duplicative in structure with H008 (same deficiency-mimic logic, weaker evidence base) and neither new nor repurposing. Revise to specify the interventional design concretely — repletion dose, target 25(OH)D level, shedding/density endpoints, and a comparator — or fold it into a single combined micronutrient-correction hypothesis with H008.

### 17. LEVOTHYROXINE (H035)

- ChEMBL: CHEMBL1624 | Elo 1516 | confidence 3/5 | route: oral | origin: generation (round 3)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: the endocrine mimic within the diffuse-thinning presentation - patients (predominantly women) with confirmed hypothyroidism (elevated TSH) whose diffuse shedding is telogen effluvium, not true androgen-driven DUPA. Thyroid hormone is required for normal hair-matrix proliferation and anagen maintenance; hypothyroidism increases telogen shedding and shedding severity. TSH-gated levothyroxine replacement to biochemical euthyroidism removes a treatable driver, paralleling the ferritin-gated iron arm already in the pool.
- **Evidence:** PMID 38181279: in 500 women with telogen effluvium, the hypothyroid subgroup (n=150) had a significantly higher mean SALT score and a higher proportion of severe hair loss than euthyroid and hyperthyroid groups. Dossier section 3 lists hypo- and hyperthyroidism as specific, treatable causes of diffuse shedding. The same study notes the thyroid-TE link is still debated, so the hypothesis is gated on confirmed abnormal TSH - correction of a diagnosed deficiency state, not empirical treatment of euthyroid patients. (refs: PMID 38181279)
- **Safety:** Benign when titrated to normalize TSH in confirmed hypothyroidism. Over-replacement causes iatrogenic hyperthyroidism, which itself causes shedding plus cardiac and bone risk; hence dosing is lab-guided with periodic TSH monitoring. Never use empirically in euthyroid patients - that would be the blind-supplementation error the dossier warns against. Appropriate systemic burden for the indication when biomarker-gated.
- **Novelty rationale:** Not a novel drug, but it closes the last uncovered diagnostic-exclusion niche: the pool already has iron (H008/H028), vitamin D (H009/H013), and zinc (H010) arms, yet no incumbent addresses the thyroid mimic - the one endocrine cause the provided excerpt base directly ties to shedding severity (PMID 38181279). This is the evidence-graded mimic-capture arm the dossier asks for, not a reworded incumbent.

Reviews:
- plausibility 9/10, evidence 7/10, safety 9/10, novelty 2/10 — verdict **accept**. The one citation this bundle actually makes checks out: PMID 38181279 exists and says roughly what is claimed (retrospective study, 500 women with TE, 150 hypothyroid, significantly higher mean SALT and more severe hair loss in the hypothyroid subgroup) - no misattribution. But note what that study does NOT show: it is a cross-sectional association, not evidence that levothyroxine replacement reverses the shedding, and its own authors call the thyroid-TE link debated; the hypothesis is honest about this gating, which is to its credit. The real objection is novelty and category: treating confirmed hypothyroidism is textbook standard of care, not repurposing - this is a diagnostic-workup entry wearing a drug name, exactly like the iron/vitamin D arms it cites as precedent. That is fine for portfolio completeness (the thyroid mimic was genuinely uncovered in the pool) and the biomarker-gating avoids the blind-supplementation error the dossier warns against, but it should be tracked as workup and never compete with mechanistic candidates. Safety is excellent precisely because of the TSH gate; the only residual risk is over-replacement causing iatrogenic hyperthyroid shedding, which lab monitoring addresses.

### 18. sequential androgen-axis program for confirmed androgen-driven DUPA: topical-first dutasteride densitometry-stratified trial, with topical bicalutamide as preclinical-gated second-line escalation (H041)

- ChEMBL: n/a | Elo 1516 | confidence 3/5 | route: topical first for both stages; oral dutasteride 0.5 mg daily only as Stage-1 escalation | origin: evolution (round 3)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: densitometry/trichoscopy-confirmed true androgen-driven DUPA (miniaturization across the entire scalp including the occipital zone) after exclusion of CTE, areata incognita, endocrine, and deficiency mimics; men and women not of childbearing potential only. This merge resolves both parents' central critiques by turning their relative weaknesses into a sequencing rationale. Stage 1 - dutasteride (dual type 1/type 2 5-alpha-reductase inhibition, maximal achievable scalp DHT suppression) as first-line precisely BECAUSE it is the only androgen-axis pharmacology with proven human scalp exposure and dose-dependent DHT suppression; exposure is minimized first (topical/compounded or low-dose before oral 0.5 mg), with response judged by standardized densitometry against a predefined futility threshold, acknowledging the dossier's warning that 5AR-inhibitor response in DUPA is anecdotal and probably attenuated. The speculative type-1/occipital linkage stays dropped - the claim is maximal DHT suppression, nothing more. Stage 2 - topical bicalutamide (follicular androgen-receptor blockade, intercepting miniaturization at the level of follicle androgen susceptibility regardless of local DHT production) reserved for Stage-1 inadequate responders, and unlocked only by the parent's hard preclinical go/no-go gate: in-vitro human skin permeation, follicular concentration above the AR-binding Ki, and negligible modeled serum levels. The H002 review's molecule-choice objection is answered by the sequence itself: within this pipeline's approved-drug constraint bicalutamide is the only approved small-molecule AR antagonist with fully characterized human PK (pyrilutamide, clascoterone, fluridil are investigational or out of scope), and it is placed second-line exactly because its route is unproven while DHT suppression is proven - receptor blockade is the mechanistically orthogonal reserve, not the first bet.
- **Evidence:** No DUPA-stratified RCTs exist for either agent and none are claimed: dutasteride's approved, dose-dependent scalp DHT suppression in patterned AGA is established pharmacology extrapolated under the dossier's leading model (same androgen/DHT-AR miniaturization without regional restriction), with attenuated DUPA response explicitly expected (dossier, uncertain). Topical AR-antagonist feasibility in hair is established only as a class by investigational agents; bicalutamide has zero percutaneous or follicular data, which is why it carries a preclinical gate rather than a human rationale. No corpus citations cover the androgen axis; both reviews' evidence grading (inference from patterned AGA, no fabricated refs) is preserved. (refs: none)
- **Safety:** Exposure ordering answers the H001 systemic-burden objection: topical/low-dose dutasteride first, oral only after documented topical failure; oral 5AR inhibition carries sexual, mood, and gynecomastia effects, a ~5-week half-life, and pregnancy category X handling restrictions, restricting systemic exposure to men and women not of childbearing potential. Bicalutamide's systemic liabilities (gynecomastia, hepatotoxicity, feminization) are contained by the preclinical gate's negligible-serum-level requirement and by its second-line, men-only positioning - the H002 review's teratogenicity/female-targeting contradiction stays resolved. Local scalp tolerability is characterized in the same preclinical program before any human exposure.
- **Novelty rationale:** Materially changed from both parents by merging them into one coherent sequential strategy instead of two competing single-drug bets: the H001 review's salvage path (densitometry-stratified trial, topical/low-dose first, futility threshold) becomes Stage 1, and the H002 review's two demands (comparative molecule-choice justification, mandatory preclinical skin-PK go/no-go gate) become the gating logic of Stage 2. The new element is the sequence and its decision structure - proven-exposure DHT suppression first, receptor-level blockade as gated, orthogonal escalation for inadequate responders - which neither parent stated and which directly resolves why bicalutamide (approved, characterized) rather than its better-known topical peers (investigational, out of scope).

### 19. L-lysine (H012)

- ChEMBL: n/a | Elo 1516 | confidence 1/5 | route: oral | origin: generation (round 1)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: the iron-deficiency-associated diffuse-shedding sub-population (CTE/deficiency mimic), as an adjunct to ferritin correction rather than a standalone therapy. L-lysine is an essential amino acid that facilitates intestinal iron absorption and cellular iron uptake; the rationale is that combined L-lysine + iron repletion restores ferritin to the range associated with reduced shedding more reliably than iron alone in women with chronic diffuse telogen hair loss who respond incompletely to iron monotherapy.
- **Evidence:** The dossier lists L-lysine as an adjunct to iron utilization with rationale-based (uncertain) evidence. The iron-ferritin association it builds on is supported by PMID 16635664 (iron deficiency and hair loss relationship), PMID 20021982 (markedly lower ferritin in diffuse telogen hair loss), and PMID 32792884 (lower ferritin in diffuse hair loss vs controls). Direct lysine trial data are not in the provided material - this is an adjunct hypothesis layered on the best-supported nutritional signal. (refs: PMID 16635664, PMID 20021982, PMID 32792884)
- **Safety:** Oral L-lysine at gram-range daily doses is benign (rare GI upset); no meaningful toxicity at proposed doses. Risk profile is appropriate for a cosmetic indication. It should not be used to justify iron supplementation in non-deficient patients - the iron-gating constraints of the parent hypothesis still apply.
- **Novelty rationale:** Rationale-based with small industry-linked prior use (flagged); the specific testable claim - lysine-augmented ferritin repletion in iron-monotherapy partial responders - has not been trialed in a biomarker-stratified diffuse-loss cohort.

Reviews:
- plausibility 6/10, evidence 4/10, safety 9/10, novelty 4/10 — verdict **revise**. This hypothesis targets a DUPA mimic (iron-deficiency-associated diffuse shedding / CTE), not DUPA proper — it says so honestly, which is to its credit, but reviewers should be clear it is a nutritional-adjunct hypothesis riding on the ferritin signal, not a miniaturization therapy. PMID attribution checks out: 16635664 (iron deficiency and hair loss relationship), 20021982 (significantly lower ferritin and transferrin saturation in diffuse telogen hair loss vs controls), and 32792884 (lower ferritin in diffuse hair loss vs controls) all exist in the corpus and say roughly what is claimed. However, none of the three mentions lysine — they support the parent iron association, which the dossier itself grades as a debated causal threshold (uncertain), and the abstract of 20021982 notes 'relatively discrepant findings' across studies. The actual lysine claim — that it augments ferritin repletion in iron-monotherapy partial responders — rests on a single small industry-linked study (Rushton) that is not in the provided material and on plausibility reasoning about intestinal iron absorption; there is no direct human trial evidence that adding lysine improves hair outcomes beyond correcting iron. Weakest link: the ferritin-diffuse-loss association is correlational with a contested treatment threshold, so the whole edifice could be supplementation of non-causal biomarkers. Novelty is low: lysine+iron combinations are long-standing commercial products; only the biomarker-stratified partial-responder framing is moderately new. Safety is genuinely excellent. Recommend a ferritin-gated, stratified trial (lysine+iron vs iron alone in confirmed-deficient partial responders) and explicit exclusion of non-deficient patients.

### 20. topical dutasteride + topical fluridil combination (H027)

- ChEMBL: CHEMBL1200969 | Elo 1508 | confidence 3/5 | route: topical (both agents, compounded scalp formulations) | origin: evolution (round 2)
- **Mechanism:** Target sub-population: densitometry/trichoscopy-confirmed true androgen-driven DUPA after exclusion of CTE, areata incognita, endocrine, and deficiency mimics. The two parents attack the same androgen axis at two different levels, and merging them fixes the decisive ambiguity both reviews raised. Topical dutasteride maximally suppresses scalp DHT at the follicle (dual type 1/type 2 5-alpha-reductase inhibition) while topical fluridil saturates androgen-receptor blockade locally, hydrolyzing to an inactive metabolite on systemic absorption. The H015 reviewer objected that receptor blockade fails for the same reason 5AR inhibitors do if occipital miniaturization has a non-androgen driver; the combination converts that objection into the experiment: simultaneous maximal local DHT suppression PLUS maximal local AR blockade is the strongest testable version of the androgen-axis model. If the combination fails against objective phototrichogram endpoints, that is positive evidence for a non-androgen driver and retires the whole axis for DUPA; if it succeeds where either agent alone was attenuated, residual androgen signaling was the explanation. Exposure stays scalp-local throughout, directly answering the H001 reviewer's systemic-burden objection: no oral 5AR inhibitor anywhere in the protocol.
- **Evidence:** Both parents rest on inference from the dossier's androgen model, honestly graded: no DUPA-stratified RCTs exist and 5AR-inhibitor response in DUPA is anecdotal and probably attenuated. Dutasteride's superior scalp DHT suppression versus finasteride is established patterned-AGA pharmacology. Fluridil has only a handful of small, short, industry-linked European trials (the 2% Eucapil program, e.g., Sovak et al.) showing at best arrest of loss, and its development stalled - per the H015 review these must be cited explicitly at literature validation rather than alluded to; no PMIDs are in the provided corpus, so none are claimed here. What the combination adds is not new evidence but a decisive design: the two-level blockade makes the axis falsifiable, which neither single-agent parent could do. (refs: none)
- **Safety:** All exposure is topical, which is the point: fluridil's built-in hydrolysis deactivation limits systemic anti-androgen exposure, and topical/compounded dutasteride substantially lowers (but does not eliminate) the sexual, mood, and gynecomastia risks of oral 5AR inhibition. Pregnancy category X handling restrictions still apply to dutasteride; women of childbearing potential are excluded from dutasteride exposure. Local irritation is the main anticipated adverse effect for fluridil. Long-term fluridil data are sparse because its development program was small - acknowledged as a residual risk.
- **Novelty rationale:** Materially changed from both parents: this is a merge, not a rewording. From H001 it drops all oral exposure (fixing the systemic-burden critique) and drops the speculative type-1/occipital claim entirely. From H015 it answers the 'cuts both ways' critique by design rather than argument: the combination is positioned strictly as the adjunct/escalation experiment the reviewer demanded, with objective phototrichogram endpoints and a predefined futility threshold, and with the stalled-program history stated openly instead of glossed. No incumbent or parent proposes simultaneous upstream DHT suppression plus receptor-level blockade confined to the scalp.

Reviews:
- plausibility 6/10, evidence 3/10, safety 7/10, novelty 7/10 — verdict **revise**. No PMIDs claimed and none in the corpus - attribution is clean, but that means the evidentiary base is inference plus a handful of small, stalled, industry-linked fluridil trials. The two-level androgen blockade is genuinely the strongest testable version of the androgen-axis model for DUPA, and the falsifiability framing (combination failure retires the axis) is intellectually sound. Weakest link: delivery. 'Topical dutasteride' is not an approved formulation anywhere; compounded versions have notoriously variable scalp penetration and can produce substantial systemic DHT suppression - the claim that exposure 'stays scalp-local throughout' is asserted, not demonstrated, and undercuts the answer to the H001 systemic-burden objection unless serum DHT is a measured safety endpoint. Fluridil adds a second unproven variable: its program stalled for a reason, supply is boutique, and combining two individually-unvalidated agents makes a negative result uninterpretable (failed formulation vs failed axis). Needs a specified vehicle/formulation with documented scalp pharmacokinetics, serum DHT monitoring, and a single-agent run-in or factorial element so the decisive experiment is not confounded.

## Method summary

Hypotheses were proposed by LLM subagents grounded in a curated AGA pathway dossier, PubMed excerpts, and the ChEMBL approved-drug universe; peer-reviewed (reflection), ranked by Elo through pairwise tournaments, refined by evolution, validated against ClinicalTrials.gov, OpenTargets, and PubMed co-mention novelty, and synthesized by meta-review. The orchestration code (hairloop) is deterministic and calls no LLM.
